conflicts.description: Same Media-tab/persistent-rail conflict as course-editor-overview.json — this screen shares the showcase's single assembled mockup with Overview.
conflicts.resolution: See screens/course-editor-overview.json#/conflicts. The Curriculum tab itself (sections/lessons/reorder) is not directly affected by the Media-tab question — its own structure (section containers, lesson rows, reorder affordances) already matches the showcase's ReorderableList composition closely.

layout.structure: Tabs (Curriculum active) -> "New section title" input + "Add Section"/"Add Quiz" -> ordered ReorderableList of section containers, each with a nested ReorderableList of lessons

content: per section: title, Delete section, nested lesson ReorderableList (each lesson: title, video-attached Badge, up/down reorder), Add Lesson button, section-level up/down reorder

artworkRules: n/a — structural editing screen, no course-thumbnail artwork.

states.empty: "this course has no content yet" + CTA "Add Section"
states.error: Snackbar on failed reorder/save, retried transparently where possible

rtlBehavior: drag handle and Move Up/Down icons are non-directional (vertical), unaffected by RTL; row content (title, badges) mirrors per logical properties
responsiveRules: list stacks full-width below Desktop; nested lesson lists remain legible (indentation reduces but doesn't disappear)
accessibilityRule: every section/lesson row exposes Move Up/Move Down IconButtons in addition to the drag handle, always visible — never drag-only (design-system/COMPONENTS.md § ReorderableList)
knownGaps: D52: section-block surface color was implicit (inherited from the parent panel) rather than an explicit color.surface.default — made explicit so each section container reads as a distinct card, matching sectionList's own card-container intent. Section/lesson row structure, spacing, and reorder affordances were already spec-compliant against COMPONENTS.md § ReorderableList (verified D52) — no other change made, per 'do not change instructor authoring behavior unnecessarily.'
